src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 — No producer/consumer version-skew handling is introduced for the new required `end_timestamp_precise` field (e.g. no `.get()` fallback or schema-version branch), so this consumer deploy is only safe if all producers writing to the topic are guaranteed upgraded first; a normal rolling deploy or topic backlog of older messages will crash-loop the consumer

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 — val["end_timestamp_precise"]` uses dict-index access with no default and the field has no default in the Span NamedTuple, so any Kafka message lacking the key (old-schema producer, message produced before this field existed, or not-yet-upgraded producer during rolling deploy) raises KeyError and crashes the whole batch in process_batch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new required field `end_timestamp_precise: float` to the `Span` NamedTuple (no default) and `process_batch` now constructs `Span(..., end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"], ...)` using direct dict indexing. If any consumed Kafka message lacks this key, `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` will raise `KeyError`, causing `process_batch` to fail for the batch. No fallback (`get`) or default is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 — No producer/consumer version-skew handling is introduced for the new required `end_timestamp_precise` field (e.g. no `.get()` fallback or schema-version branch), so this consumer deploy is only safe if all producers writing to the topic are guaranteed upgraded first; a normal rolling deploy or topic backlog of older messages will crash-loop the consumer

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the consumer now unconditionally reads `end_timestamp_precise` via `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` when constructing `Span`. If older messages (or producers) don’t include this field, this will raise a `KeyError` and can crash the consumer. The diff shows no `.get(...)` fallback, defaulting, or version-branching to handle producer/consumer skew.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that organization_context.member.has_global_access is accessed without a None-check, leading to an AttributeError when the user is not a superuser and organization_context/member is missing. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (organization_context can be None causing AttributeError).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:21 — Cursor accepts arbitrary (including negative) client-supplied offsets via Cursor.from_string with no validation, and downstream paginators handle negative offsets inconsistently (silent clamp in BasePaginator vs. crash in OptimizedCursorPaginator), so the same cursor contract behaves differently depending on which paginator class is active

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces/permits negative offsets (Cursor.offset comment in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py, and logic in src/sentry/api/paginator.py). Handling is inconsistent between paginator paths: BasePaginator’s get_result clamps to >=0 only when not cursor.is_prev (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), while OptimizedCursorPaginator, when `enable_advanced_features` is set, will pass a negative `start_offset` directly into queryset slicing (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Since Cursor offsets are not validated in the shown code, the same cursor can behave differently depending on which paginator is active, and the optimized path can attempt an invalid negative slice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced short-circuits only for is_superuser; for a non-superuser, organization_context.member can be None (e.g. superuser-less non-member access paths), so .has_global_access would raise AttributeError

adjudication.rationale: In organization_auditlogs.py the new line `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` unconditionally dereferences `organization_context.member` when the user is not a superuser. The diff itself does not establish that `organization_context.member` is always non-None for this endpoint, so the reported AttributeError path cannot be definitively verified, but the added logic does introduce a concrete null-safety edge-case risk that should be guarded (e.g., `getattr(organization_context.member, "has_global_access", False)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Redirect-chain depth limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 (and the explanatory comment about broken joins was deleted) with no stated relation to the eviction feature, materially increasing the chance that deep segment trees fail to join correctly

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-following loop was reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with a comment noting that very deep trees may fail to join) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no other compensating logic. The loop is what resolves `set_span_id` by repeatedly following `hget` redirects; if a redirect chain exceeds 1000 hops, the loop will terminate without reaching the true root, causing `set_span_id` to be incorrect and potentially preventing correct segment joining. The new eviction logic later in the script (zset trimming to 1000 spans) does not address redirect-chain depth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 — val["end_timestamp_precise"] is accessed with a hard subscript (no .get/default) unlike the other optional fields, so any inbound span message lacking this key (e.g. during a producer/consumer schema rollout) raises KeyError and fails the whole batch

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the diff adds a new required `Span` field `end_timestamp_precise` (in `buffer.py`) and populates it via `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]`. Unlike other fields (`parent_span_id`, `is_remote`) which use `.get(...)`, this will raise `KeyError` if an inbound message lacks the key. The diff itself does not show any guarding/backward-compat handling for older producers or mixed-schema rollouts; tests were updated to always include the field, reinforcing that the consumer will now hard-fail on missing data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The new `zpopmin` eviction that silently drops spans once a segment exceeds 1000 members emits no metric/log and the dropped count (`span_count - 1000`) is never returned to Python (`add_buffer.lua` return tuple unchanged), so this partial data-loss path is completely unobserved compared to the previous `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric/log it replaces

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua` the new cap (`if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`) will drop spans silently: there is no metric/log emission in the Lua script, and on the Python side the prior observability for “too many spans” was removed (`segment_span_count_exceeded` metric + error log block in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` was deleted). The claim about the dropped count not being returned to Python is not verifiable from this diff (the Lua return value isn’t shown), but the lack of any replacement instrumentation for this partial-eviction path is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449 — The old max_segment_spans guard (drop oversized segment, log error, increment segment_span_count_exceeded metric) was deleted from flush_segments with no test removed/added to reflect that overflow now silently truncates via Lua zpopmin instead of dropping+logging the whole segment

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `max_segment_spans` overflow guard in `_load_segment_data` was removed: the prior block that checked `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`, incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded`, logged an error, and dropped the segment was deleted when switching from `sscan` to `zscan` (payloads now extend from `zscan_values`). Separately, `add-buffer.lua` now enforces a hard cap by truncating the sorted set to 1000 entries via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`, meaning overflow behavior changed from "drop+log+metric" at flush-time to "truncate" at write/merge-time. The diff does not add/adjust tests to cover this changed overflow behavior or the removed metric/log path, so the finding is a concrete review concern but not necessarily a functional defect.
